turns.content: In a labeled convex hexagon whose six boundary sides are red and whose diagonals are red or blue, characterize which vertex triples are automatically safe and which can form an all-blue triangle.
List all vertex triples whose three connecting edges are diagonals and therefore require a constraint.
For each constrained triple, count the colorings of its three diagonals with at least one red edge, and determine whether the two diagonal sets overlap.
Identify diagonals not used by the automatically safe triples and count their independent colorings.
Multiply the independent constrained-triangle and free-diagonal factors for the labeled hexagon.
Check that every other triangle contains at least one red boundary side and that no quotient by rotational symmetry is intended.
Report the number of valid labeled diagonal colorings.
